Funding sequence

FS-01 / The order

The same five applications, sent in the wrong order, get declined.

The banks you use and the order you use them in decide how much money you get. Most companies submit everything at once.

  • Look at this. It's section three of the lender list we print for every client, and the first line of that section says it: applying to the wrong lender first burns hard inquiries and triggers automatic declines that follow you to the next application.
  • Same five applications. Same file. In the wrong order, they get declined.
  • The banks you use and the order you use them in decide how much money you get.
  • Most companies submit everything at once, to one list of lenders they use for every single client.
  • That's how a good file walks away with a report full of hard inquiries.
  • We plan the order first. These five rules print on every copy of your documents, and the rest of this deck walks them.

FS-02 / Personal first

Your personal file goes first, then each business on its own.

  • Nothing else is worth doing until your personal file is ready.
  • Each business is judged on its own. Then it's round after round.
  • Walk the order with me.
  • Your personal file goes first. Nothing else is worth doing until it's ready.
  • Then personal funding. Personal comes before business, every time.
  • Then business one, on its own. Then business two, on its own. A bank judges each business by itself, after your personal file is ready.
  • If you don't have a business yet, you skip that step and go straight to the lender list.
  • And then the applications keep going, round after round. That's a funding sequence.

FS-03 / One at a time

One application at a time, so the inquiries never stack up.

  • Every application leaves a hard inquiry, and the next bank reads it on your report.
  • The banks see the inquiries stack, and they start denying you. It's called inquiry stacking.
  • So we wait for the decision before the next application goes out. Never shotgun applications.
  • Here's rule three, straight off the report: wait for the decision before you send the next one. Never shotgun applications.
  • Every application leaves a hard inquiry. The next bank sees it on your report.
  • When they stack up, the banks start denying you. That's inquiry stacking.
  • So one goes out, we wait for the bank's answer, then the next one goes out.
  • There's no fixed wait between two banks. The decision sets the pace.
  • A blast sends them all at once. A plan sends one, waits, then sends the next.

FS-04 / Which banks

National banks first, then banks in your state, then banks in your business's state.

  • Every bank on your list is picked from your file, so you only apply where your file makes sense.
  • Where you live and where your business is each open their own local banks, and the list reads in that order.
  • Which banks go first? Look at the three bands.
  • National banks first. Then the local banks in the state you live in. Then the local banks in the state your business is in.
  • Each bank on that list is picked from your file, so you only apply where your file makes sense.
  • Where you live opens one set of local banks. Where your business is opens another. That's why we ask for both.
  • The bank decides, not us. We pick the banks and the order. They say yes or no.

FS-05 / Rounds and sweeps

Between rounds, we dispute the new hard inquiries.

  • We apply in rounds. One funding sequence is about six rounds.
  • Inside a round, the pulls are spread across the three bureaus, and a bank that pulls a bureau with a fresh inquiry on it is held back.
  • Between rounds, we dispute the new hard inquiries, so the next round starts from a cleaner file. That's how a funding sequence builds real capital.
  • Walk the line with me. Round one goes out.
  • Inside that round, the pulls are spread across the three bureaus, so no single bureau gets stacked.
  • Then, before the next round goes out, we dispute every new hard inquiry, so the next round starts from a cleaner file.
  • One funding sequence is about six rounds. Round, sweep, round, sweep.
  • Your file goes into each round clean. That's how a funding sequence builds real capital.
  • And the applying keeps going, sequence after sequence.
